A1.justification: Both PDFs describe TextRegion. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and appendices are readable and support reliable matching despite reformatting and additional material in v2.

before.justification: v1 reports original TextRegion results for semantic segmentation, referring expression comprehension and multi-object grounding, together with component ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds mask-generator comparisons and qualitative results.

M1.justification: Mask-based attention pooling, global-patch filtering, multi-resolution encoding and prediction procedures are unchanged. Appendix A.3 retains the same SigLIP2 and Perception Encoder adaptations. Alternative mask generators are evaluated as ablations of the existing framework.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same six segmentation datasets, three RefCOCO-family datasets and Reasoning Segmentation dataset. The added mask comparisons and qualitative examples remain within these existing tasks and data coverage.

E2.justification: Table 1 substantially expands the ViT-B/16 comparison with ResCLIP, LaVG, LPOSS+ and CLIPtrase, while removing CLIP Surgery. It also removes MaskCLIP from the OpenCLIP ViT-H/14 comparison, although MaskCLIP remains under ViT-B/16. Comparator membership in Tables 2 and 3 is unchanged.

E3.justification: The new Table 9 introduces a controlled comparison of ground-truth, SLIC, SAM and SAM2 masks using ViT-B/16 encoders on COCO-Stuff and ADE20K. Existing benchmark settings and metrics remain unchanged. The explicit statement that TextRegion uses FGVP's proposal set clarifies the existing referring-expression evaluation rather than establishing a changed protocol.

E4.justification: Section 5 adds a substantive mask-quality ablation across three encoder families and two datasets, testing the framework's dependence on its segmentation input and performance with annotated masks. Figure 6 adds corresponding visual comparisons, while Appendix A.5 adds segmentation and referring-expression case studies, including boundary and semantic failures. Earlier ablations are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. The additional experiments retain point-estimate reporting.

E6.justification: Substantial new evidence comes from the added baseline results and mask-quality study. Table 1 now reports CLIPtrase at 44.2 on COCO-Object versus TextRegion's unchanged 41.1. Table 9 adds CLIP COCO-Stuff results of 36.5 with ground-truth masks, 21.3 with SLIC and 27.9 with SAM, alongside the retained SAM2 value of 28.7. Previously reported scores are unchanged; new qualitative results are also added, and the flag-grounding example is replaced by an antler-grounding example.

T1.justification: Equations 1–7 and their mathematical reasoning are retained, with no added proofs or formal results. Correcting the mask-stack shape from H×W to R×H×W clarifies notation for the already-described collection of R masks.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution bullets and conclusion retain the same claims: training-free text-aligned region tokens, strong zero-shot performance and compatibility across image-text encoders and mask inputs. The expanded introduction and new experiments explain and support these existing claims.

C2.justification: Section 5 adds an interpretation that global-patch interference is less severe in CLIP than in SigLIP2 and Perception Encoder. Appendix A.5 explains errors involving intricate object contours and misinterpreted referring expressions. These make the existing general limitations concerning mask quality and language understanding more concrete.

D1.justification: Section 4.2 explicitly confirms use of the same object proposals as FGVP, and the acknowledgements newly identify NVIDIA GPU resources at NCSA Delta. The code link, Appendix A.2 hyperparameters, encoder adaptations and query-generation instructions remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds references for SLIC, LaVG, LPOSS, ResCLIP, ClearCLIP and VisionZip, and removes the CLIP Surgery reference. Overall research positioning remains stable. Section 2 introduces citation mismatches: ClearCLIP points to a SCLIP bibliography entry, while CLIPtrase points to ClearCLIP.

P1.justification: v2 expands the introduction's motivation, adds localized discussion and Appendix A.5, and supplies explicit appendix cross-references. Most existing prose and the section sequence are retained. Publication and affiliation text, citation style and some notation are also revised.

P2.justification: The document is comprehensively reformatted into the TMLR layout, changing typography, margins, headers and display placement. Table 1 is expanded, Tables 5–8 move from a compact block beside prose to a horizontal row, and Table 9 plus Figures 6, 9 and 10 are added. Earlier appendix figures are renumbered, with one example replaced and legends adjusted.

improvement.justification: The broader comparisons and new mask-quality ablation strengthen evidence for the existing framework, while Appendix A.5 makes its failure modes clearer. These are useful extensions to an already substantial evaluation; the method and previous scores remain unchanged. Removed comparator rows and newly mismatched related-work citations modestly offset the gains, leaving a limited overall improvement.
